title: Production software keeps breaking and it will only get worse — Anish Agarwal, Traversal.ai
talk_summary: A vendor pitch from Traversal.ai arguing that AI-written code makes production troubleshooting the bottleneck, and that incident debugging needs causal ML + reasoning models + parallel agent swarms rather than runbooks or single ReAct loops.

takeaways.technique: Parallel fan-out search instead of sequential tool loops
takeaways.what_they_do: On incident start, spawn many parallel agent tool calls to exhaustively search telemetry, then aggregate into ranked root-cause candidates with confidence levels, rather than one agent iterating tool-by-tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: traversal AI orchestrates a swarm of expert AI sRes to sift through pabytes of observability data all in parallel
takeaways.numbers: ~40% MTTR reduction claimed at Digital Ocean; results returned in ~5 minutes

takeaways.technique: Ranked candidates with confidence + citations, not a single verdict
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one answer, the system returns multiple root-cause candidates each with cited evidence, a confidence level, and reasoning, so a human can verify quickly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It cites relevant observability data just like any good engineer would. It gives you confidence levels for the potential root cause candidates.

takeaways.technique: Don't dump raw logs into context; search-then-cite
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues LLMs can't ingest terabytes of logs and lack numerical understanding, so the system must select the microscopic relevant evidence first and pass only that, with citations.

takeaways.technique: Skip static runbooks; derive next step from live state
takeaways.what_they_do: Claims runbooks are stale the moment they're written, so agents should not depend on a fixed meta-workflow for choosing the next tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: any runbook you actually put into place is deprecated the second you create it

takeaways.technique: Latency budget as a design constraint
takeaways.what_they_do: Sets a hard target of resolving incidents in 2-5 minutes, which rules out unbounded agent loops that could run for days.
takeaways.evidence_quote: typically if you try to solve an incident, you need to solve it in two to five minutes for it to be really useful
